deny.reason: force push is disabled in this sandbox; use --force-with-lease if you must overwrite a remote ref you expect, or ask the operator to run it.
force push is disabled in this sandbox; use --force-with-lease if you must overwrite a remote ref you expect, or ask the operator to run it.
hard reset is disabled in this sandbox; it discards uncommitted work. Use `git stash` or commit first, or ask the operator.
bypassing commit/push hooks is disabled in this sandbox; fix the hook failure instead of skipping it.
reflog expire is disabled in this sandbox; it removes the safety net the reflog gives you.
stash drop is disabled in this sandbox; it discards stashed work irreversibly. Use `git stash pop` if you want it back.

git -c is disabled in this sandbox; it can override any config key, including ones that run arbitrary commands (core.pager, credential.helper, ...). Edit .git/config directly if you need a persistent change. (prefix, not contains: -c is a global flag and only ever valid as argv[0]; this also stops it from wrongly catching -c as a *subcommand's own* flag, e.g. `git switch -c`, `git branch -c`, `git commit -c HEAD`.)
git --config-env is disabled in this sandbox for the same reason -c is: it can override any config key, sourced from an environment variable this sandbox does not otherwise expose to argv inspection.

git config is disabled in this sandbox, reads included; writing config (or defining an alias) from here can install something that reaches a denied command with no shim in the way at all — e.g. `git config alias.h 'reset --hard'` then `git h`, or `git config credential.helper ...`. Read $WORKDIR/.git/config directly if you only need to inspect it, or ask the operator for a persistent change.
git branch -D (force-delete) is disabled in this sandbox; it discards a branch's commits without checking they are merged anywhere else. Use `git branch -d`, or ask the operator.
rewriting history with git filter-branch is disabled in this sandbox; it rewrites every commit it touches, effectively irreversibly for anything already pushed or referenced elsewhere.
rewriting history with git filter-repo is disabled in this sandbox; it rewrites every commit it touches, effectively irreversibly for anything already pushed or referenced elsewhere.
git update-ref -d is disabled in this sandbox; it deletes a ref directly, bypassing the normal branch/tag-delete paths and their own safety checks.
git update-ref --delete is disabled in this sandbox; it deletes a ref directly, bypassing the normal branch/tag-delete paths and their own safety checks.
git gc --prune=now is disabled in this sandbox; it immediately discards unreachable objects, including ones a mistaken hard reset or stash drop would otherwise still let you recover from the reflog.
git gc --prune=all is disabled in this sandbox; it immediately discards unreachable objects, including ones a mistaken hard reset or stash drop would otherwise still let you recover from the reflog.
changing a git remote is disabled in this sandbox; it can silently redirect where a future push or fetch goes. Ask the operator.
